entry.name: mc.chord~
entry.digest: Store and Recall Signal Values Associated with an Index
entry.description: The mc.chord~ object is something like a version of the Max coll object that generates audio signals. You can store lists (which you can think of as chords) of numbers associated with a unique index, then recall your lists with messages or signals. When recalled, list values are assigned to channels in a multi-channel signal according to one of several allocation modes.

arguments.name: channels
arguments.description: Ansupplied as an argument sets the initial output channel count.

attributes.name: allocmode
attributes.digest: Allocation Mode
attributes.description: Determine how list values are allocated to channels

choices.label: WHenis set to Lowest (0), list items are output starting with the first item allocated to the first output channel.
WHenis set to Highest (1), list items are output starting with the first item allocated to the last output channel, the second item to the second-to-last channel, etc.

choices.digest: Assign to least recently used channels
choices.label: Whenis set to Cyclic (2), list items are assigned to least recently used channels in ascending order.
Whenis set to Random (3), list items are assigned to randomly chosen channels.

attributes.description: Determines a signal change for increment index

choices.digest: Trigger changes on zero to non-zero transitions
choices.label: Whenis set to Zero to Non-Zero (0), signal changes for incrementing the index of the output (whenis set to Increment Index) are defined as the previous sample being zero and the current sample being non-zero.

Whenis set to Change (1), signal changes for incrementing the index of the output (whenis set to Increment Index) are defined as any difference between the value of the previous and current samples in the input signal.

messages.digest: Delete a list associated with an index
messages.description: The wordfollowed by an index deletes a list of values associated with that index.

messages.name: dictionary
messages.description: Whenreceives ain the proper format, it will replace all stored lists with those in the dictionary. Data must be in the form of an array of dictionaries associated with the key. Each dictionary has the keywith the index to associate with the list, followed by a list of values associated with the key.

messages.name: int
messages.description: Anoutputs the list associated with the number as a multi-channel signal out the left outlet. If no list was stored at this number, zero signals are output.

messages.name: list
messages.description: stores the items starting at the second value at an index specified by the first value. Example:will store the listat index 5.

messages.name: signal
messages.digest: Output matching lists based on signal values
messages.description: Whenis set to Lookup (0), the signal value is truncated to an integer. When this integer value changes,checks whether it matches an index for a stored list; if so, it outputs the associated list as a multi-channel signal.Whenis set to Increment Index (1), any change in the value of the input signal will cause the next stored list to be output in a cyclic fashion.

messages.name: store
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a list argument, stores the items in the list starting at the second value at an index specified by the first value. Example:will store the listat index 5.

inlets.description: A signal connected torecalls stored lists according to the current. You can also store or recall values using messages.

outlets.description: A multi-channel signal containing the values of the most recently recalled list. The assignment of list values to channels is set by theattribute. Ifis set to zero, unused channels will be set to zero, otherwise they contain values from previously recalled lists.
If a channel in the left outlet is currently allocated to a list value, the corresponding channel in the second outlet will be 1, otherwise it will be 0.

When a stored list inis recalled, it will be sent out the third outlet. The order of the list is the order the values were initially stored, which may not correpond to the order they appear in the channels of the left outlet depending on the current setting of.
When a list is recalled, its index is sent out the right outlet.
